findings.text: An upstream that dies mid-body is recorded as completed. status is set to STATUS_COMPLETED as soon as the upstream answers 2xx (router.py:581-582), before the body loop; an exception out of next_chunk.result() (router.py:604) escapes the inner handler, which rewrites the status only for asyncio.CancelledError (router.py:620), and the finally at 626 writes the row anyway. Concrete input (repro_upstream_cut.py): the engine answers 200 with content-length 4096, writes one SSE chunk, then aborts its transport. The caller receives ClientPayloadError (Response payload is not completed) while the appended row reads status=completed, prompt_tokens=None, completion_tokens=None, time_to_first_token_s=0.000468. A truncated relay therefore lands in the load and cost stream as a successful request, against the section's own clause that a failed or aborted request is recorded as such rather than dropped. One-line fix: set STATUS_FAILED in the inner handler before re-raising.

Requests the router answers itself leave no receipt, including a failing one. The 404 path for an unrouted POST and the locally served catalog GET both return before _relay (whose sole call site is router.py:291-300), so no row can be appended (router.py:241-246, 244-277). Concrete input (repro_unrecorded_requests.py): POST /v1/chat/completions with {"model": "nope"} is answered 404 by the router and GET /v1/models is answered 200 from the merged catalogs; afterwards the receipts file does not exist and 0 rows were written. Against every completed request through the router appears once in the stream this leaves the router's own answers out. A row per catalog GET would be noise, but a 404 the router generates is a request the stream could carry honestly, and a router-answered failure is exactly what the failed-or-aborted clause names. Coordinator judgement; the node's tests neither assert nor exclude it.

The sampling ceiling has no operator surface. RequestReceiptSink(self._receipts_path) is the sole production construction and passes neither max_rows_per_s nor window_s, so the 20 rows/s ceiling and 1 s window from request_receipts.py:54-55 are fixed by source. The rate the writer used is stamped on every kept row, so a reader is never misled, and the plan's above the configured rate reads as satisfied in code; but no launch, document or CLI surface can raise the ceiling for a campaign that wants full fidelity without editing the module. Minor: the fix is one parameter threaded through create_router_app/serve_router, which already carry request_receipts_path.

justifications.durability: Every behaviour the suite pins survives an independent mutation control run against the reviewed tests unmodified (mutation_plugin.py; logs mutation_feed.log 3 failed, mutation_sample.log 2 failed, mutation_write.log 7 failed, each including the assertion its clause names). The unwritable-destination guard is shown refusing rather than present: it latches _write_failed permanently, logs once, and the relay still completes. Docked for the untested production derivation (lane_document to requests.jsonl) and for the unreachable sampling knobs, which are durable in the wrong direction.
justifications.evidence: Everything claimed was re-derived rather than read from the manifest: 16 passed for tests/test_request_receipts.py plus tests/test_agent_router.py, ruff check imas_ambix tests exit 0, serving-interpreter parse gate 2 passed, and git hash-object agreement across the worktree, the reviewed commit and main HEAD proving which revision was reviewed. The gate's latency figure is taken on pytest tmp_path (xfs) while production writes to gpfs; re-measured here at p99 69.2 and 144.3 us over 200 rows (max 6.0 ms once), under the 1 ms budget. Docked because the p99 assertion covers sink and parse work rather than the router's added latency through the relay, because the aborted and failed assertions do not reach the mid-stream cut that F1 names, and because the guard test asserts the log line appears rather than that it appears once.
justifications.fit: Follows the repository's own habits: frozen slots dataclass, frozenset path dispatch, the benchmark's parse mirrored by assertion rather than re-derived (bench.py:683-694), the sink constructed beside the lane document, tests extending the existing router harness, no new dependency, and no launch change. Docked for F3 and for _caller_hint embedding the ephemeral client port, which limits grouping by caller (pre-existing, not introduced here).
justifications.goal_fidelity: The section's goal lands: one append-only row per relayed request carrying the named fields, the aborted and failed paths recorded rather than dropped, honest sampling fractions stamped on kept rows, its own stream, and a path derived from the endpoint document so production needs no wiring change (confirmed at cli.py:1591-1596). Docked for F1 and F2, each of which narrows a done-when clause to its relayed-request case: a truncated relay counts as completed, and requests the router answers itself never appear.
justifications.scope_discipline: Each declared write path was touched for its stated purpose; nothing else in the tree changed. The plan edit is one r-comment block appended at section 6 with the plan-* meta scalars unchanged, both commits carry conventional subjects with bodies and no attribution, and no plan label, ticket reference, version suffix or author name appears in any source name, comment or docstring (flagged hits were API paths and the model name). The one path outside the declared five, docs/figures/request-receipts/receipt-overhead.png, is required by the landing contract in the dispatch template itself and was disclosed in the plan comment, so it is recorded as a template tension rather than a node defect.

- Read in full: the three changed source files, the tests/test_agent_router.py harness, bench.py::_stream_chat (the parse the design reuses), cli.py::serve_router (the production construction), and docs/plans/serve-telemetry-spine.html sections 6 and 7.

GATE RE-DERIVED (not taken from the manifest)
- pytest tests/test_request_receipts.py tests/test_agent_router.py -> 16 passed
- ruff check imas_ambix tests -> All checks passed, exit 0
- serving-interpreter parse gate -> 2 passed
- Latency assumption re-measured on the production filesystem. The gate writes to pytest tmp_path (xfs) while production resolves to <home>/public/imas-ambix/requests.jsonl (gpfs). 200 rows per target: xfs median 30.4 us p99 52.1 us; gpfs run 1 median 33.8 us p99 144.3 us max 6023.7 us; gpfs run 2 median 32.5 us p99 69.2 us max 768.4 us. Under the 1 ms p99 budget, so the clause holds; the single 6 ms gpfs outlier is worth knowing, not a breach.

CHECKLIST
1. Done-when clauses against assertions. Every completed request appears once is asserted by test_every_relayed_request_writes_one_fully_populated_row (5 requests in, 5 rows out, every field populated); a failed or aborted request is recorded as such is asserted for a caller disconnect (aborted) and an upstream 500 (failed); sampling above the configured rate records its fraction is asserted twice (fraction kept, and kept rows self-describing); the lint gate exits 0. Two gaps, each reproduced: an upstream that dies mid-body is recorded as completed (F1), and requests the router answers itself leave no row at all, including a 404 (F2). The latency clause is asserted (p99 < 0.001) over sink and parse work rather than through the relay, narrower than the clause, though the independent measurement above shows the budget holds.
2. Knobs at their call sites. request_receipts_path reaches the sink through cli.py:1591-1596 (serve_router passes lane_document, from which router.py:185-199 derives the receipts path) - verified at the call site, so receipts land beside the endpoint document with no launch change. max_rows_per_s and window_s reach the sampling decision and the stamped row rate, but router.py:646 is the only production construction and passes neither (F3).
3. Guards shown refusing. The unwritable-destination guard is shown refusing in test_an_unwritable_destination_cannot_disturb_the_relay: the sink latches _write_failed, logs once, and the relay still completes. The truncated-body guard refuses rather than answering confidently (HEAD_BYTES bound, asserted by test_a_truncated_body_is_not_read_as_a_confident_wrong_answer). Runtime mutation controls, reviewed tests unmodified: feed -> 3 failed including the fully-populated row; sample -> 2 failed including the fraction assertion; write -> 7 failed including the unwritable-destination test. Each pinned behaviour has at least one assertion that fails when the behaviour is broken, so the guards are load-bearing.
4. Naming and attribution. Ran the naming checks over the changed files: no plan label, gate ID, ticket reference, version suffix or author attribution in any name, comment or docstring. The only flagged strings are false positives - API paths such as /v1/messages/count_tokens and the model name DeepSeek-V4.1. Both reviewed commits carry a conventional subject and a body, and no AI attribution.
5. Negative control. Not armed for the reviewed node: negative_control appears 0 times in its prompt.txt and negative_control_log 0 times in its manifest.md, so there is no declared mutation to check and the item is not applicable. Recorded as evidence rather than scored as a pass.

FINDINGS
F1 imas_ambix/agent/router.py:581-604 with :620 - an upstream cut mid-body is recorded as completed. Reproduced by repro_upstream_cut.py; the caller raises ClientPayloadError while the row says status=completed with null token figures.
F2 imas_ambix/agent/router.py:239-277 - requests the router answers itself (404 for an unknown model, 200 catalog GET) leave zero rows and no file, reproduced by repro_unrecorded_requests.py.
F3 imas_ambix/agent/router.py:646 - the sampling ceiling is fixed by source; no operator surface can move it. Minor.

OUT OF SCOPE (reported, not triaged)
F1 and F2 are fix nodes' work; this node changed no code. The dispatch template's landed-figure contract and its FENCE SCOPE path list disagree (the figure path is outside the five declared paths), which is a template tension rather than a node defect.
